name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q01 - Basis of classification used by Aristotle

questiontext.text: Which criterion was primarily used by Aristotle to divide plants into trees, shrubs, and herbs?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the historical classification attempt
Aristotle was the earliest scientist to attempt a more scientific basis for biological classification.

Step 2: Recall Aristotle's criteria for plants
To classify plants into trees, shrubs, and herbs, Aristotle used simple morphological characters rather than internal anatomy or evolutionary lineage.

Step 3: Evaluate other criteria
Phylogenetic relationships and cellular details like cell walls were introduced in much later systems by scientists such as Whittaker.

Final Conceptual Answer: Aristotle classified plants into trees, shrubs, and herbs based on simple morphological characters.

answer.text: Simple morphological characters
Complex anatomical features
Presence or absence of cell wall
Phylogenetic evolutionary relationships

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q02 - Division of animals according to Aristotle

questiontext.text: Aristotle classified animals into two distinct groups on the basis of which of the following features?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall Aristotle's classification of animals
In his scientific classification, Aristotle observed the nature of blood in various animal groups.

Step 2: Identify the specific diagnostic criterion
He divided animals into two groups: those that had red blood and those that did not.

Step 3: Distinguish from modern criteria
Modern concepts such as notochord, coelom, and symmetry were developed much later in animal taxonomy.

Final Conceptual Answer: Aristotle divided animals into two groups based on the presence or absence of red blood.

answer.text: Mode of locomotion and habitat
Presence or absence of red blood
Presence or absence of notochord
Body symmetry and coelom type

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q03 - Inadequacy of two kingdom classification system

questiontext.text: The two-kingdom classification system proposed by Linnaeus was found inadequate primarily because it failed to distinguish between:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyse the two-kingdom system
Linnaeus classified all living organisms into two kingdoms: Plantae and Animalia.

Step 2: Identify its fundamental deficiencies
This system grouped bacteria, fungi, algae, and higher plants together under Plantae simply due to the presence of a cell wall. Consequently, it did not distinguish prokaryotes from eukaryotes, unicellular from multicellular forms, or photosynthetic autotrophs (green algae) from heterotrophs (fungi).

Step 3: Conclude the primary basis of inadequacy
The failure to separate prokaryotic/eukaryotic, unicellular/multicellular, and autotrophic/heterotrophic organisms made the two-kingdom system scientifically inadequate.

Final Conceptual Answer: The two-kingdom system was inadequate because it did not distinguish between prokaryotes and eukaryotes, unicellular and multicellular organisms, and photosynthetic and non-photosynthetic organisms.

answer.text: Terrestrial organisms and aquatic organisms possessing distinct physiological adaptations
Flowering plants and non-flowering plants based on their reproductive mechanisms
Prokaryotes and eukaryotes, unicellular and multicellular organisms, and photosynthetic and non-photosynthetic organisms
Vertebrate animals and invertebrate animals based on skeletal organisation

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q04 - Main criteria used in Whittaker classification

questiontext.text: Which of the following sets of characteristics represents the main criteria used by R.H. Whittaker for his Five Kingdom Classification?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the Five Kingdom Classification proposal
R.H. Whittaker proposed the Five Kingdom Classification in 1969, comprising Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.

Step 2: Identify Whittaker's primary classification criteria
Whittaker formulated his classification based on five broad biological criteria: cell structure (prokaryotic vs eukaryotic), body organisation (cellular vs tissue/organ), mode of nutrition (autotrophic vs heterotrophic absorptive/ingestive), reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships.

Step 3: Differentiate from superficial parameters
Superficial characters like gross habitat or simple geographical distribution were not the core criteria.

Final Conceptual Answer: Whittaker's main criteria were cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships.

answer.text: Gross morphology, habitat, chromosome number, and geographical distribution
Cell wall composition, presence of flagella, reserve food, and respiratory pigment
Embryological stages, presence of coelom, body symmetry, and locomotion
Cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q05 - Organization of the three domain system

questiontext.text: In the three-domain system of classification, the Kingdom Monera is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the three-domain concept
The three-domain system divides cellular life into three primary domains based on fundamental molecular differences.

Step 2: Trace the division of Monera
Kingdom Monera is split into two distinct domains (Archaea and Bacteria), recognising the profound differences between archaebacteria and eubacteria.

Step 3: Account for the remaining kingdoms
All the eukaryotic kingdoms (Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia) are placed together in the third domain (Eukarya), resulting in a six-kingdom scheme.

Final Conceptual Answer: The three-domain system divides Kingdom Monera into two domains, leaving all remaining eukaryotic kingdoms in the third domain.

answer.text: Kept intact in one domain, while Plantae and Animalia form the other two domains
Divided into three separate domains based on cell wall composition alone
Divided into two domains, while all eukaryotic kingdoms are placed in the third domain
Merged with Kingdom Protista to form a single prokaryotic domain

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q06 - Unifying character in earlier plant classifications

questiontext.text: In earlier classification systems, bacteria, blue-green algae, fungi, mosses, ferns, gymnosperms, and angiosperms were all grouped under 'Plants' because they all shared:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the historical definition of the Plant Kingdom
In earlier systems, such as the two-kingdom system, diverse organisms were classified under Kingdom Plantae.

Step 2: Identify the single unifying morphological criterion
The single unifying feature used was that all these organisms possessed an outer cell wall covering their cells.

Step 3: Recognise the limitation of this criterion
This criterion overlooked profound differences in cellular organisation (prokaryotic vs eukaryotic) and nutrition (heterotrophic fungi vs autotrophic plants).

Final Conceptual Answer: Earlier systems placed bacteria, fungi, algae, and plants together because all of them possessed a cell wall.

answer.text: The presence of a cell wall in their cells
Autotrophic mode of nutrition through photosynthesis
Eukaryotic cellular organisation with membrane-bound organelles
A multicellular body organisation with true tissue differentiation

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q07 - Reclassification of unicellular algae into Protista

questiontext.text: Under Whittaker's five-kingdom classification, Chlamydomonas and Chlorella were removed from algae under plants and placed in Kingdom Protista together with Paramoecium and Amoeba because:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Examine the previous classification
Earlier classifications placed Chlamydomonas and Chlorella in algae under Plantae (because they have cell walls and are photosynthetic), while Paramoecium and Amoeba were placed under Animalia (because they lack cell walls and are heterotrophic).

Step 2: Apply Whittaker's criteria
Whittaker defined Kingdom Protista as the kingdom encompassing all unicellular eukaryotic organisms.

Step 3: Analyze the outcome of the shift
Since Chlamydomonas, Chlorella, Paramoecium, and Amoeba are all unicellular eukaryotes, they were brought together into Kingdom Protista, demonstrating how revised criteria resolve morphological anomalies.

Final Conceptual Answer: Whittaker placed Chlamydomonas and Chlorella in Protista because all unicellular eukaryotes are grouped together under Kingdom Protista.

answer.text: They share an identical heterotrophic mode of nutrition and lack photosynthetic pigments
They possess prokaryotic cellular organization without any membrane-bound organelles
They completely lack cell walls similar to animal cells
All unicellular eukaryotic organisms are grouped under Kingdom Protista regardless of cell wall presence

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q08 - Chemical composition of moneran cell wall

questiontext.text: According to the characteristics of the five kingdoms, the cell wall of organisms belonging to Kingdom Monera is composed of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Consult the diagnostic features of Kingdom Monera
Monerans are prokaryotic organisms lacking a nuclear envelope.

Step 2: Recall the chemical nature of the moneran cell wall
Unlike plant cell walls made of cellulose or fungal walls containing chitin, the moneran cell wall is non-cellulosic, formed of polysaccharides and amino acids (peptidoglycan).

Step 3: Confirm against other kingdoms
Plantae has cellulosic walls, Fungi has chitinous walls, and Animalia lacks a cell wall completely.

Final Conceptual Answer: The cell wall of Kingdom Monera is non-cellulosic, composed of polysaccharides and amino acids.

answer.text: Cellulose embedded with pectin and lignin
Non-cellulosic material consisting of polysaccharides and amino acids
Chitin and fungal cellulose
Silica embedded in a double-layered protein framework

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q09 - Body organisation characteristic of Kingdom Fungi

questiontext.text: Which level of body organisation is characteristically exhibited by Kingdom Fungi according to the five-kingdom system?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review body organisation across Whittaker's five kingdoms
Monera and Protista display cellular organisation; Plantae shows tissue/organ level; Animalia exhibits tissue/organ/organ system levels.

Step 2: Identify fungal body organisation
Fungi possess multicellular bodies made of hyphae, forming a mycelium that represents a multicellular or loose tissue level of organisation rather than true organs.

Step 3: Conclude the characteristic level
Loose tissue/multicellular structure is the defined organisation for Kingdom Fungi.

Final Conceptual Answer: Kingdom Fungi exhibits a multicellular or loose tissue level of body organisation.

answer.text: Strictly cellular level of organisation with no intercellular interaction
Multicellular or loose tissue organisation
Organ system level of organisation with coordinated internal cavities
True organ level of organisation with differentiated vascular bundles

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q10 - Morphological categories of bacteria by shape

questiontext.text: Comma-shaped bacteria and spiral-shaped bacteria are respectively designated as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the four basic shapes of bacteria
Bacteria are grouped into four categories based on their external morphology: spherical Coccus, rod-shaped Bacillus, comma-shaped Vibrio, and spiral-shaped Spirillum.

Step 2: Match the requested shapes
The comma-shaped bacterium is called Vibrio (plural: vibrio), and the spiral-shaped bacterium is called Spirillum (plural: spirilla).

Step 3: Eliminate incorrect pairings
Bacillus is rod-shaped and Coccus is spherical.

Final Conceptual Answer: Comma-shaped bacteria are Vibrio and spiral-shaped bacteria are Spirillum.

answer.text: Bacillus and Coccus
Coccus and Vibrio
Spirillum and Bacillus
Vibrio and Spirillum

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q11 - Metabolic diversity within Kingdom Monera

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements regarding the metabolic characteristics of bacteria is correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand bacterial structure versus behaviour
Structurally, bacteria are very simple prokaryotic cells lacking membrane-bound organelles.

Step 2: Evaluate their metabolic range
In behaviour and metabolism, bacteria as a group show the most extensive metabolic diversity among living organisms.

Step 3: Differentiate nutritional modes
Some bacteria are autotrophs (photosynthetic or chemosynthetic), while the vast majority are heterotrophs (saprophytes or parasites).

Final Conceptual Answer: Bacteria possess simple cellular structure but exhibit the most extensive metabolic diversity as a group.

answer.text: Bacteria show very simple structural organisation but the most extensive metabolic diversity as a group
Bacteria show highly complex cellular structures but uniform autotrophic nutrition
All bacteria are obligate heterotrophs dependent on decaying organic substrates
Photosynthetic bacteria rely exclusively on organic substrates for carbon fixation

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q12 - Predominant nutritional mode among bacteria

questiontext.text: The vast majority of bacteria obtain their nutrition as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review nutritional categories in bacteria
Bacteria include both autotrophs (synthesising food from inorganic substrates) and heterotrophs.

Step 2: Identify the relative abundance
Although autotrophy is present, the vast majority of bacteria are heterotrophs that depend on other living organisms or on dead organic matter for food.

Step 3: Conclude the primary mode
Heterotrophy (saprophytic or parasitic) represents the dominant nutritional mode among bacteria.

Final Conceptual Answer: The vast majority of bacteria are heterotrophs that depend on other organisms or dead organic matter for food.

answer.text: Chemosynthetic autotrophs oxidising inorganic nitrites and nitrates
Photosynthetic autotrophs utilising sunlight and water as electron donor
Heterotrophs depending on other organisms or dead organic matter
Obligate endosymbionts residing within plant root nodules

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q13 - Structural basis of archaebacterial extreme survival

questiontext.text: What structural feature is primarily responsible for the survival of archaebacteria under extremely harsh environmental conditions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the characteristics of archaebacteria
Archaebacteria thrive in extreme habitats such as high salt (halophiles), hot springs (thermoacidophiles), and marshy areas (methanogens).

Step 2: Identify the physiological adaptation
Archaebacteria differ from eubacteria in having a distinct cell wall structure, which provides thermal and osmotic resilience.

Step 3: Connect structure to function
This unique cell wall architecture is specifically responsible for their survival under extreme environmental stresses.

Final Conceptual Answer: A different cell wall structure is responsible for the survival of archaebacteria in extreme environments.

answer.text: The presence of a thick mucilaginous capsule containing photosynthetic pigments
The formation of resistant endospores containing low-molecular-weight RNA
The presence of eukaryotic-like histone proteins wrapped around plasmids
A distinct and specialized cell wall structure differing from other bacteria

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q14 - Habitat and ecological function of methanogens

questiontext.text: Methanogens belong to archaebacteria and are characteristically found in:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the group methanogens
Methanogens are anaerobic archaebacteria living in marshy habitats and animal digestive tracts.

Step 2: Recall their association with ruminants
They reside in the rumen (gut) of ruminant animals including cows and buffaloes.

Step 3: Identify their metabolic product
They convert organic compounds into methane (biogas), which is released from the dung of these animals.

Final Conceptual Answer: Methanogens occur in the gut of ruminants such as cows and buffaloes and produce biogas from dung.

answer.text: Hot sulphur springs where they oxidise hydrogen sulphide to sulphate
Hyper-saline water bodies where they form thick pinkish surface blooms
The gut of ruminant animals such as cows and buffaloes, producing biogas from dung
Deep ocean trenches where they fix nitrogen into nitrates

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q15 - Photosynthetic pigment present in cyanobacteria

questiontext.text: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) are classified as photosynthetic autotrophs because they possess:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Examine the photosynthetic apparatus of cyanobacteria
Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic autotrophic eubacteria.

Step 2: Identify their primary photosynthetic pigment
They possess chlorophyll a, which is identical to the chlorophyll a present in higher green plants.

Step 3: Confirm photosynthetic mechanism
Because they have chlorophyll a and perform oxygenic photosynthesis, they are autotrophic true bacteria.

Final Conceptual Answer: Cyanobacteria possess chlorophyll a similar to green plants.

answer.text: Bacteriochlorophyll and bacterioviridin
Chlorophyll a similar to green plants
Chlorophyll b and fucoxanthin
Phycocyanin without any chlorophyll pigments

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q16 - Role of specialized heterocysts in cyanobacteria

questiontext.text: In cyanobacteria like Nostoc and Anabaena, specialized cells called heterocysts are primarily adapted for:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the organism and structure
Nostoc and Anabaena are filamentous cyanobacteria that possess specialized thick-walled cells known as heterocysts.

Step 2: Determine the biochemical function
Heterocysts provide an anaerobic micro-environment required by the nitrogenase enzyme to fix atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia.

Step 3: Conclude the primary role
Thus, heterocysts function specifically in atmospheric nitrogen fixation.

Final Conceptual Answer: Specialized heterocysts in Nostoc and Anabaena function in fixing atmospheric nitrogen.

answer.text: Fixation of atmospheric nitrogen
Asexual reproduction through endogenous spore formation
Absorption of water and mineral nutrients from damp soil
Oxidation of inorganic sulphur for ATP synthesis

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q17 - Nutrient recycling by chemosynthetic bacteria

questiontext.text: Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria obtain energy for ATP production and play an essential ecological role in recycling:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand chemosynthetic autotrophy
Chemosynthetic autotrophs do not utilise light energy; instead, they oxidise various inorganic substrates like nitrates, nitrites, and ammonia.

Step 2: Trace energy capture
The chemical energy released during these oxidation reactions is trapped to produce ATP for cellular synthesis.

Step 3: Identify nutrient cycling role
Through these oxidative pathways, chemosynthetic bacteria play a key role in recycling crucial biogeochemical nutrients, specifically nitrogen, phosphorus, iron, and sulphur.

Final Conceptual Answer: Chemosynthetic autotrophs oxidise inorganic substances to generate ATP and recycle nitrogen, phosphorus, iron, and sulphur.

answer.text: Nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, iron, and sulphur by oxidising inorganic substances
Atmospheric oxygen by photolysing water molecules during sunlight exposure
Organic glucose into lactic acid under anaerobic soil conditions
Cellulose in dead plant debris into humic acids and biogas

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q18 - Identification of bacterial plant and animal diseases

questiontext.text: Which of the following groups contains only diseases caused by pathogenic bacteria?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review diseases mentioned in the text under eubacteria
Pathogenic heterotrophic bacteria cause major diseases in humans, crops, farm animals, and pets.

Step 2: Verify the pathogen for each candidate disease
Cholera is caused by Vibrio cholerae (bacterium), typhoid by Salmonella Typhi (bacterium), tetanus by Clostridium tetani (bacterium), and citrus canker by Xanthomonas axonopodis (bacterium).

Step 3: Identify non-bacterial diseases in distractors
Mumps, smallpox, herpes, and AIDS are viral diseases; malaria and sleeping sickness are protozoan diseases; potato spindle tuber is caused by a viroid.

Final Conceptual Answer: Cholera, typhoid, tetanus, and citrus canker are all bacterial diseases.

answer.text: Mumps, smallpox, influenza, and herpes
Cholera, potato spindle tuber, malaria, and tetanus
Cholera, typhoid, tetanus, and citrus canker
Citrus canker, sleeping sickness, typhoid, and AIDS

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q19 - Distinctive cellular and metabolic characteristics of Mycoplasma

questiontext.text: Which combination of features correctly describes Mycoplasma?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the defining traits of Mycoplasma
Mycoplasma are unique prokaryotes placed under Kingdom Monera.

Step 2: Check structural and physiological features
They completely lack a cell wall, represent the smallest known free-living cellular entities, and are facultative anaerobes that can survive without oxygen.

Step 3: Review pathogenicity
Many mycoplasmas are pathogenic in animals and plants.

Final Conceptual Answer: Mycoplasmas completely lack a cell wall, are the smallest living cells known, and can survive without oxygen.

answer.text: Organisms with a rigid peptidoglycan cell wall that are obligate aerobes
Organisms that completely lack a cell wall, are the smallest living cells known, and can survive without oxygen
Filamentous prokaryotes surrounded by a mucilaginous sheath that fix nitrogen
Acellular nucleoproteins possessing an inert crystalline protein coat

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q20 - Ambiguity in boundaries of Kingdom Protista

questiontext.text: Why are the boundaries of Kingdom Protista considered not well-defined?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the composition of Protista
Protista includes single-celled eukaryotes such as chrysophytes, dinoflagellates, euglenoids, slime moulds, and protozoans.

Step 2: Examine taxonomic overlap
Because many unicellular protists have chloroplasts and perform photosynthesis (like dinoflagellates and euglenoids), some botanists treat them as unicellular plants, while general biologists classify them as protists.

Step 3: Note the textbook statement
The text states explicitly: 'the boundaries of this kingdom are not well defined. What may be a photosynthetic protistan to one biologist may be a plant to another.'

Final Conceptual Answer: The boundaries of Kingdom Protista are not well-defined because what is a photosynthetic protistan to one biologist may be viewed as a plant by another.

answer.text: Protists contain both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cellular organisations simultaneously
Some protists lack genetic material and reproduce only by protein aggregation
Protists are exclusively multicellular organisms showing organ-level body differentiation
What is considered a photosynthetic protistan by one biologist may be considered a plant by another

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q21 - Cell wall structure and deposit of diatoms

questiontext.text: In diatoms, the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells that fit together as in a soap box and are indestructible because they are embedded with:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the organism group
Diatoms belong to Chrysophytes in Kingdom Protista.

Step 2: Recall wall architecture
Their cell wall consists of two thin overlapping valves/shells fitting together like a soap box.

Step 3: Identify the chemical impregnating the wall
The wall matrix is embedded with silica, making it chemically inert and indestructible, leading to vast accumulations called diatomaceous earth.

Final Conceptual Answer: The indestructible cell walls of diatoms are embedded with silica.

answer.text: Chitin
Silica
Cellulose and pectin
Calcium carbonate

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q22 - Ecological status and commercial applications of diatoms

questiontext.text: Which organisms are recognized as the chief 'producers' in the oceans, whose gritty accumulated soil is used in polishing and filtration?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the ocean's chief primary producers
Diatoms (chrysophytes) carry out a major portion of oceanic photosynthesis and are designated as the chief 'producers' in the oceans.

Step 2: Connect with diatomaceous earth uses
Over billions of years, their silica cell walls accumulated as diatomaceous earth, which has a gritty texture used commercially in polishing and the filtration of oils and syrups.

Final Conceptual Answer: Diatoms are the chief producers in the oceans, and their accumulated deposits are used in polishing and filtration.

answer.text: Diatoms
Dinoflagellates
Euglenoids
Cyanobacteria

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q23 - Flagellar orientation in typical dinoflagellates

questiontext.text: Most dinoflagellates possess two flagella that are positioned in which specific orientation?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall dinoflagellate morphology
Dinoflagellates are mostly marine, photosynthetic protists with stiff cellulose plates in their cell walls.

Step 2: Detail the flagellar arrangement
They typically possess two heterokont flagella: one flagellum lies longitudinally while the other lies transversely in a groove or furrow between the cellulosic wall plates.

Step 3: Contrast with euglenoids and ciliates
One short and one long flagellum in an anterior pocket is typical of euglenoids, whereas rows of cilia are characteristic of ciliated protozoans.

Final Conceptual Answer: Dinoflagellates have one longitudinal flagellum and one transverse flagellum lying in a furrow between the wall plates.

answer.text: Both flagella are inserted apically and beat symmetrically in an anterior direction
One flagellum is short and the other is long, both arising from an anterior invagination
One flagellum lies longitudinally and the other lies transversely in a furrow between the wall plates
Thousands of tiny flagella are arranged in coordinated longitudinal rows along the cell surface

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q24 - Causative agent and impact of red tides

questiontext.text: The phenomenon of 'red tides' in the sea is caused by rapid multiplication of which organism, and what is its ecological consequence?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the organism responsible for red tides
Red tides are caused by the rapid multiplication (population blooms) of red dinoflagellates, notably Gonyaulax.

Step 2: Understand the ecological effect
The immense population tints the sea red and secretes large quantities of potent toxins into the water.

Step 3: Identify the consequence
These released toxins can cause mass mortality of marine animals, including fishes.

Final Conceptual Answer: Red tides are caused by rapid multiplication of Gonyaulax, whose toxins can kill other marine animals such as fishes.

answer.text: Trichodesmium, which enriches the ocean with nitrogen to promote fish growth
Euglena, which produces an oily pellicle that reduces dissolved oxygen
Physarum, which forms a giant plasmodium engulfing marine plankton
Gonyaulax, which produces toxins that can kill marine animals such as fishes

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q25 - Flexibility and mixotrophic nutrition in euglenoids

questiontext.text: Which of the following features distinguishes euglenoids from other photosynthetic protists?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Examine the body covering of euglenoids
Instead of a rigid cellulosic cell wall, euglenoids possess an elastic, protein-rich outer layer called the pellicle, which gives flexibility to the body.

Step 2: Examine their nutritional behaviour
Euglenoids are mixotrophic: they photosynthesise in the presence of sunlight (with pigments identical to higher plants), but when deprived of light, they behave as heterotrophs by predating on smaller organisms.

Step 3: Contrast with diatoms and dinoflagellates
Diatoms have silica shells, dinoflagellates have cellulose plates, whereas euglenoids lack a cell wall entirely.

Final Conceptual Answer: Euglenoids lack a cell wall, have a protein-rich pellicle that makes them flexible, and exhibit mixotrophic nutrition.

answer.text: Presence of an indestructible silica-embedded cell wall with saprophytic nutrition
Presence of stiff cellulosic plates with obligate chemotrophic nutrition
Multicellular coenocytic body covered by a chitinous exoskeleton
Absence of a cell wall, presence of a protein-rich pellicle, and mixotrophic nutrition

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q26 - Spore characteristics of slime moulds under adversity

questiontext.text: During unfavourable conditions, the plasmodium of slime moulds differentiates into fruiting bodies bearing spores. These spores are notable because they:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand slime mould life cycle under stress
Under unfavourable environmental conditions, the aggregated vegetative body (plasmodium) differentiates to form fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips.

Step 2: Analyze spore anatomy and durability
Unlike the vegetative plasmodium which lacks a cell wall, the spores possess true walls. These walls provide extreme resistance, enabling them to survive adverse conditions for many years.

Step 3: Note the mode of dispersal
The spores are eventually dispersed by air currents.

Final Conceptual Answer: Spores of slime moulds possess true walls, are extremely resistant, and survive adverse conditions for many years.

answer.text: Lack cell walls, are flagellated, and swim actively in dew droplets
Possess true walls, are extremely resistant, and survive adverse conditions for many years
Contain silica-embedded shells that fit together as in a soap box
Are produced exogenously and dispersed exclusively by water currents

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q27 - Characteristics of marine amoeboid protozoans

questiontext.text: Which of the following characteristics is true for marine forms of amoeboid protozoans?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review amoeboid protozoans
Amoeboid protozoans live in freshwater, seawater, or moist soil, moving and capturing prey using pseudopodia.

Step 2: Identify the specific marine adaptation
Marine amoeboids characteristically develop silica shells on their surface for protection and structural support.

Step 3: Contrast with other protozoans
Cilia occur in ciliated protozoans, flagella in flagellated forms, and infectious spore stages in sporozoans.

Final Conceptual Answer: Marine amoeboid protozoans possess silica shells on their surface.

answer.text: They possess silica shells on their surface
They possess two flagella lying in longitudinal and transverse furrows
They possess thousands of coordinated cilia directing food into a gullet
They possess an infectious spore-like stage in their life cycle

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q28 - Feeding mechanism in ciliated protozoans

questiontext.text: In Paramoecium, water laden with food is steered into the gullet primarily due to:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the anatomy of Paramoecium
Paramoecium is a ciliated protozoan possessing thousands of cilia and a distinct cavity (gullet) opening to the exterior.

Step 2: Understand the ciliary feeding mechanism
The coordinated, rhythmic beating of rows of cilia drives water currents carrying food particles directly into the gullet.

Step 3: Conclude the responsible mechanism
The coordinated movement of cilia is the sole active mechanism steering food into the gullet.

Final Conceptual Answer: Coordinated movement of rows of cilia steers food-laden water into the gullet in Paramoecium.

answer.text: The rapid whiplash movement of a single anterior flagellum
The extension and contraction of blunt pseudopodia
The coordinated movement of rows of thousands of cilia
The passive suction created by an expanding contractile vacuole

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q29 - Defining feature of the sporozoan group

questiontext.text: Which feature unifies all organisms categorized as sporozoans, exemplified by Plasmodium?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the diagnostic trait of sporozoans
Sporozoans are endoparasitic protozoans lacking specialized locomotory organelles like cilia or flagella.

Step 2: Recognize their life cycle characteristic
They are unified by the presence of an infectious spore-like stage in their life cycle.

Step 3: Connect to Plasmodium
Plasmodium (the malarial parasite) produces sporozoites, representing this infectious spore-like stage.

Final Conceptual Answer: Sporozoans are unified by having an infectious spore-like stage in their life cycle.

answer.text: Presence of pseudopodia for locomotion and phagocytosis
Possession of a pellicle and mixotrophic photosynthetic mode
Presence of an infectious spore-like stage in their life cycle
Possession of two heterokont flagella and cellulose plates

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q30 - Causative agent of sleeping sickness

questiontext.text: Sleeping sickness in humans is caused by a flagellated protozoan known as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify flagellated protozoans
Flagellated protozoans are free-living or parasitic protozoans that possess flagella.

Step 2: Recall the parasitic example
The parasitic member Trypanosoma causes the serious human disease sleeping sickness.

Step 3: Distinguish from other protozoans
Entamoeba is an amoeboid parasite, Plasmodium is a sporozoan parasite, and Paramoecium is a free-living ciliated protozoan.

Final Conceptual Answer: Trypanosoma is the flagellated protozoan causing sleeping sickness.

answer.text: Entamoeba
Plasmodium
Paramoecium
Trypanosoma

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q31 - Nature of coenocytic hyphae in fungi

questiontext.text: In certain fungi, the hyphae are continuous tubes filled with multinucleated cytoplasm without cross-walls. Such hyphae are termed:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the structure of fungal hyphae
Fungal bodies are composed of slender filaments called hyphae.

Step 2: Distinguish between hyphal types
Some hyphae possess cross walls or septa dividing them into cells (septate hyphae). Others lack septa and form continuous tubes filled with multinucleate cytoplasm.

Step 3: Define the terminology
These aseptate, multinucleated hyphae are specifically termed coenocytic hyphae.

Final Conceptual Answer: Continuous hyphae filled with multinucleated cytoplasm are called coenocytic hyphae.

answer.text: Septate hyphae
Coenocytic hyphae
Dikaryotic hyphae
Haustorial hyphae

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q32 - Chemical constituents of fungal cell wall

questiontext.text: The cell walls of fungi are characteristically composed of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall fungal cell biology
Unlike plants whose cell wall is primarily cellulose, fungi possess a distinct wall composition.

Step 2: Identify the components
The cell walls of fungi are composed of chitin (a polymer of N-acetylglucosamine) and polysaccharides.

Step 3: Eliminate other alternatives
Peptidoglycan is bacterial; silica is diatomaceous; pure cellulose is typical of green plants.

Final Conceptual Answer: The cell walls of fungi are composed of chitin and polysaccharides.

answer.text: Chitin and polysaccharides
Cellulose and pectin
Peptidoglycan and lipopolysaccharides
Silica and glycoproteins

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q33 - Sequential events in fungal sexual reproduction

questiontext.text: Which of the following represents the correct sequential order of the three steps involved in the sexual cycle of fungi?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the initial event of sexual reproduction
First, the protoplasms of two compatible motile or non-motile gametes fuse; this step is called plasmogamy.

Step 2: Identify the second event
Following plasmogamy, the two haploid nuclei fuse to form a diploid nucleus; this step is called karyogamy.

Step 3: Identify the third event
Finally, reduction division (meiosis) occurs in the diploid zygote, yielding haploid spores.

Step 4: Establish the sequence
Therefore, the sequence is Plasmogamy, followed by Karyogamy, followed by Meiosis in the zygote.

Final Conceptual Answer: The sexual cycle of fungi follows the sequence: Plasmogamy, Karyogamy, and Meiosis in zygote.

answer.text: Plasmogamy -> Karyogamy -> Meiosis in zygote
Karyogamy -> Plasmogamy -> Meiosis in zygote
Meiosis in zygote -> Plasmogamy -> Karyogamy
Plasmogamy -> Meiosis in zygote -> Karyogamy

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q34 - Occurrence of dikaryotic stage in fungal classes

questiontext.text: In which classes of fungi does an intervening dikaryotic stage (n + n, two nuclei per cell) occur between plasmogamy and karyogamy?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the dikaryon condition
In some primitive fungi, plasmogamy is followed immediately by nuclear fusion (karyogamy) yielding diploid (2n) cells.

Step 2: Trace where dikaryophase is prolonged
In Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes, karyogamy is delayed after plasmogamy. This results in an intervening condition with two unfused haploid nuclei per cell (n + n), known as a dikaryon.

Step 3: Contrast with Phycomycetes
In Phycomycetes, fusion of compatible gametes directly produces a zygospore without a prolonged dikaryotic phase.

Final Conceptual Answer: An intervening dikaryotic stage occurs in Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes.

answer.text: Phycomycetes and Ascomycetes
Phycomycetes and Basidiomycetes
Phycomycetes and Deuteromycetes
Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q35 - Diagnostic features and examples of Phycomycetes

questiontext.text: Which set of features is characteristic of members of Phycomycetes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review mycelial structure of Phycomycetes
Phycomycetes are lower fungi found in aquatic habitats, decaying wood, or as obligate plant parasites. Their mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic.

Step 2: Review asexual reproduction
Asexual reproduction occurs via zoospores (motile) or aplanospores (non-motile), which are produced endogenously within a sporangium.

Step 3: Contrast with higher fungi
Higher fungi (ascomycetes and basidiomycetes) have septate, branched mycelia and produce exogenous asexual conidia or lack asexual spores.

Final Conceptual Answer: Phycomycetes have aseptate, coenocytic mycelium and endogenously produced asexual spores in a sporangium.

answer.text: Branched and septate mycelium with exogenously produced conidia on conidiophores
Branched and septate mycelium with exogenously produced basidiospores on a basidium
Aseptate and coenocytic mycelium with endogenously produced asexual spores in a sporangium
Septate mycelium that completely lacks any known asexual spore production

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q36 - Parasitic fungus causing white spots on mustard

questiontext.text: The parasitic fungus responsible for white spots seen on mustard leaves belongs to Phycomycetes and is named:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the disease and host
White spots on mustard leaves are caused by a parasitic fungus belonging to the class Phycomycetes.

Step 2: Recall the genus
This organism is Albugo (specifically Albugo candida).

Step 3: Differentiate from other parasitic fungi
Puccinia causes wheat rust, Ustilago causes smut, and Neurospora is an ascomycete used in genetics.

Final Conceptual Answer: Albugo is the parasitic fungus causing white spots on mustard leaves.

answer.text: Puccinia
Albugo
Ustilago
Neurospora

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q37 - Origin and site of spore formation in Ascomycetes

questiontext.text: In Ascomycetes, the asexual spores (conidia) and sexual spores (ascospores) are produced respectively in which manner?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze asexual spore formation in Ascomycetes
Asexual reproduction in ascomycetes occurs via conidia, which are pinched off exogenously at the tips of specialized hyphae called conidiophores.

Step 2: Analyze sexual spore formation in Ascomycetes
Sexual reproduction yields ascospores, which develop endogenously inside sac-like structures called asci (singular: ascus).

Step 3: Confirm the respective orientations
Therefore, conidia are produced exogenously on conidiophores, while ascospores are produced endogenously in asci.

Final Conceptual Answer: Conidia are formed exogenously on conidiophores, and ascospores are formed endogenously in sac-like asci.

answer.text: Endogenously in sporangia and exogenously on basidia
Exogenously on conidiophores and endogenously in sac-like asci
Endogenously in asci and exogenously on conidiophores
Exogenously on basidiocarps and endogenously in ascocarps

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q38 - Fungal genus extensively used in genetic research

questiontext.text: Which member of Ascomycetes is extensively utilized in biochemical and genetic research?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review Ascomycetes members
Ascomycetes include Aspergillus, Claviceps, Neurospora, and Penicillium.

Step 2: Identify the model organism for genetics
Neurospora (often termed the Drosophila of the fungal kingdom) is extensively used in biochemical and genetic work.

Step 3: Connect to NCERT text
The text explicitly states: 'Neurospora is used extensively in biochemical and genetic work.'

Final Conceptual Answer: Neurospora is extensively used in biochemical and genetic research.

answer.text: Claviceps
Penicillium
Neurospora
Aspergillus

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q39 - Plasmogamy and basidiospore formation in Basidiomycetes

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes reproduction in Basidiomycetes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate sex organs and plasmogamy in Basidiomycetes
In Basidiomycetes, distinct sex organs are completely absent. Plasmogamy is brought about by the fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains.

Step 2: Trace the resulting dikaryon and basidium
This fusion creates a dikaryotic mycelium that gives rise to a basidium. Inside the basidium, karyogamy and meiosis occur.

Step 3: Determine number and orientation of basidiospores
Meiosis produces four haploid basidiospores that are borne exogenously on the basidium.

Final Conceptual Answer: Basidiomycetes lack sex organs, undergo plasmogamy via somatic fusion, and produce four basidiospores exogenously on the basidium.

answer.text: Sex organs are absent, plasmogamy occurs by somatic cell fusion, and four basidiospores are formed exogenously on the basidium
Sex organs are well-developed, and four basidiospores are formed endogenously inside each basidium
Asexual reproduction by flagellated zoospores is common, producing motile basidiospores
Plasmogamy is immediately followed by meiosis without any dikaryotic stage

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q40 - Members of the fungal class Basidiomycetes

questiontext.text: Smut and rust diseases in plants are caused by which members of Basidiomycetes respectively?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify smut fungus
Smut disease is caused by Ustilago, a member of Basidiomycetes.

Step 2: Identify rust fungus
Rust disease (such as wheat rust) is caused by Puccinia, also a member of Basidiomycetes.

Step 3: Confirm correct pairing order
Ustilago is the smut fungus and Puccinia is the rust fungus.

Final Conceptual Answer: Smut is caused by Ustilago and rust is caused by Puccinia.

answer.text: Puccinia and Ustilago
Albugo and Alternaria
Colletotrichum and Claviceps
Ustilago and Puccinia

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q41 - Reason for designating Deuteromycetes as imperfect fungi

questiontext.text: Deuteromycetes are commonly known as 'imperfect fungi' because:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the definition of imperfect fungi
In mycology, the 'perfect' stage of a fungus refers to its sexual reproductive phase.

Step 2: Trace the limitation in Deuteromycetes
Members of Deuteromycetes are placed in this class because only their asexual or vegetative phases have been observed and described.

Step 3: Understand subsequent reclassification
When their sexual (perfect) stages are discovered, they are moved to Ascomycetes or Basidiomycetes.

Final Conceptual Answer: Deuteromycetes are called imperfect fungi because only their asexual or vegetative phases are known.

answer.text: They completely lack cell walls and reproduce only through budding
They are coenocytic and lack any known mechanism of spore dispersal
Only the asexual or vegetative phases of these fungi are known
They are incapable of decomposing organic litter and cannot cycle minerals

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q42 - Deuteromycetes examples and role in mineral cycling

questiontext.text: Which of the following sets of fungi belongs to Deuteromycetes, playing a significant role in decomposing litter and mineral cycling?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the members of Deuteromycetes
Examples given in NCERT for Deuteromycetes are Alternaria, Colletotrichum, and Trichoderma.

Step 2: Connect with their ecological function
A large number of deuteromycetes are active decomposers of litter, thereby playing a major role in mineral cycling.

Step 3: Eliminate other classes
Mucor/Rhizopus are Phycomycetes; Aspergillus/Claviceps are Ascomycetes; Agaricus/Ustilago are Basidiomycetes.

Final Conceptual Answer: Alternaria, Colletotrichum, and Trichoderma belong to Deuteromycetes and function as decomposers in mineral cycling.

answer.text: Mucor, Rhizopus, and Albugo
Alternaria, Colletotrichum, and Trichoderma
Aspergillus, Claviceps, and Neurospora
Agaricus, Ustilago, and Puccinia

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q43 - Partially heterotrophic insectivorous and parasitic plants

questiontext.text: Which of the following pairs correctly exemplifies an insectivorous plant and a plant parasite respectively?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review nutritional exceptions in Kingdom Plantae
Although plants are predominantly autotrophic, a few members are partially heterotrophic.

Step 2: Identify insectivorous plants
Bladderwort and Venus fly trap are insectivorous plants that trap insects to obtain nitrogen.

Step 3: Identify parasitic plants
Cuscuta is a parasitic angiosperm lacking chlorophyll that derives nutrients from its host.

Final Conceptual Answer: Bladderwort is an insectivorous plant and Cuscuta is a parasitic plant.

answer.text: Cuscuta and Venus fly trap
Albugo and Bladderwort
Venus fly trap and Puccinia
Bladderwort and Cuscuta

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q44 - Nutrition mode and food storage in Kingdom Animalia

questiontext.text: Members of Kingdom Animalia are characteristically heterotrophic, digest food internally, and store their food reserves primarily as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall characteristics of Kingdom Animalia
Animals are multicellular, eukaryotic heterotrophs lacking cell walls.

Step 2: Identify their nutritional mode
They ingest food and digest it within an internal cavity (holozoic nutrition).

Step 3: Identify reserve food materials
Surplus energy is stored in the form of glycogen or fat, whereas plants store reserve food as starch.

Final Conceptual Answer: Members of Kingdom Animalia store food reserves as glycogen or fat.

answer.text: Glycogen or fat
Starch and oil droplets
Mannitol and laminarin
Cellulose and pectin

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q45 - Historical discovery and nature of viruses

questiontext.text: Match the scientist with their correct discovery regarding viruses:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review Ivanowsky's contribution (1892)
Dmitri Ivanowsky recognised that causal agents of tobacco mosaic disease passed through bacteria-proof filters, showing they were smaller than bacteria.

Step 2: Review Beijerinck's contribution (1898)
M.W. Beijerinck demonstrated that the extract of infected tobacco plants caused infection in healthy plants, named the pathogen 'virus', and called the fluid 'Contagium vivum fluidum' (infectious living fluid).

Step 3: Review Stanley's contribution (1935)
W.M. Stanley demonstrated that viruses could be crystallised and that crystals consist largely of proteins.

Final Conceptual Answer: M.W. Beijerinck demonstrated that extract of infected plants could infect healthy plants and called it Contagium vivum fluidum.

answer.text: Dmitri Ivanowsky showed that viruses could be crystallised and consist largely of proteins
W.M. Stanley recognised that tobacco mosaic pathogens passed through bacteria-proof filters in 1892
T.O. Diener showed that viruses are obligate parasites possessing double-stranded DNA capsids
M.W. Beijerinck demonstrated that infected plant extract could infect healthy plants and termed it Contagium vivum fluidum

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q46 - Nature of viral genetic material and capsid

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements regarding the genetic material of viruses is correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall general viral nucleic acid rule
A virus contains either RNA or DNA as its genetic material; no virus contains both.

Step 2: Distinguish nucleic acids based on host type
In general, viruses infecting plants possess single-stranded RNA (ssRNA). Viruses infecting animals possess single- or double-stranded RNA or double-stranded DNA.

Step 3: Identify bacteriophage genome
Bacterial viruses (bacteriophages) usually possess double-stranded DNA (dsDNA).

Final Conceptual Answer: No virus contains both RNA and DNA; plant viruses generally have single-stranded RNA, whereas bacteriophages typically have double-stranded DNA.

answer.text: No virus contains both RNA and DNA; plant viruses generally possess single-stranded RNA, while bacteriophages usually possess double-stranded DNA
All viruses contain both single-stranded RNA and double-stranded DNA simultaneously inside the capsid
Bacteriophages exclusively possess single-stranded RNA protected by a polysaccharide sheath
Plant-infecting viruses invariably possess double-stranded DNA enclosed by a lipid bilayer

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q47 - Characteristics and discovery of viroids

questiontext.text: In 1971, T.O. Diener discovered viroids as new infectious agents causing potato spindle tuber disease. Viroids differ from viruses in being:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the discovery of viroids
T.O. Diener discovered viroids in 1971 as causal agents of potato spindle tuber disease.

Step 2: Contrast structural composition with viruses
Viruses consist of genetic material (RNA or DNA) enclosed within a protein coat (capsid). Viroids consist only of free, naked RNA without any protein coat.

Step 3: Note the molecular weight
The RNA of viroids is characteristically of low molecular weight.

Final Conceptual Answer: Viroids consist of free, low-molecular-weight RNA that completely lacks a protein coat.

answer.text: Infectious proteins of high molecular weight lacking genetic material
Free circular double-stranded DNA surrounded by a lipid membrane
Free infectious RNA of low molecular weight lacking a protein coat
Infectious nucleoproteins containing both RNA and capsomeres

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BIOLOGICAL_CLASSIFICATION_MCQ_Q48 - Nature of prions and symbiotic lichens

questiontext.text: Which of the following pairs correctly identifies the nature of prions and the biological significance of lichens?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Define prions and their diseases
Prions are infectious neurological agents consisting of abnormally folded proteins (similar in size to viruses). They cause bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE or mad cow disease) in cattle and Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) in humans.

Step 2: Define lichens and their ecological significance
Lichens are mutualistic symbiotic associations between an autotrophic alga (phycobiont) and a heterotrophic fungus (mycobiont). Because they are highly sensitive to pollution (such as sulphur dioxide), they do not grow in polluted areas and serve as excellent pollution indicators.

Step 3: Combine the verified concepts
Prions are abnormally folded infectious proteins causing BSE and CJD, while lichens are mutualistic associations acting as pollution indicators.

Final Conceptual Answer: Prions are abnormally folded infectious proteins causing BSE and CJD, while lichens are symbiotic bioindicators that do not grow in polluted areas.

answer.text: Prions are infectious naked DNA molecules causing scrapie; lichens are parasitic fungi destroying green algal blooms in polluted water
Prions are abnormally folded infectious proteins causing BSE and CJD; lichens are symbiotic associations that do not grow in polluted areas
Prions are low-molecular-weight RNAs causing neurological plaques; lichens are autotrophic plants thriving in high sulphur dioxide environments
Prions are crystalline viral capsids lacking nucleic acids; lichens are decomposers that digest bedrock using mycorrhizal hyphae
